title: Expressive limits: well-ordering and finite reachability
summary: Use compactness to show that well-ordering and connectedness cannot be first-order axiomatized, and finite reachability has no uniform first-order definition.
abstract: A first-order formula can say that two points are joined by a walk of three steps. Why can no single formula say that some finite walk joins them, with no fixed bound on its length? Compactness exposes the difference between each finite requirement and all of them together. The same method shows that no set of first-order axioms describes exactly the well-orders, or exactly the connected undirected graphs. Even allowing infinitely many axioms does not overcome these limits when the description must work on all nonempty structures. These examples show how to test whether a familiar class of structures or relation can be captured by first-order logic.

based_on.title: Lecture Notes: An Introduction to Model Theory
